test_title: SSC Selection Post 2025 (Graduate Level) Official Paper (Held On: 30 Jul, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The profit made on an item sold for ₹2200 is equal to the loss incurred when it is sold for ₹1800. What will be the profit or loss percentage if the item is sold for ₹2050?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Profit of 2.5%**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the **Profit** on one price equals the **Loss** on another, the **Cost Price (CP)** is the average of the two selling prices.

**CP** = (2200 + 1800) ÷ 2 = ₹2000

New **Selling Price (SP)** = ₹2050

**Profit** = 2050 − 2000 = ₹50

**Profit %** = (50 ÷ 2000) × 100 = 2.5%

**∴ The correct answer is Profit of 2.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

SP₁ = ₹2200 | SP₂ = ₹1800 | New SP = ₹2050

**Formula Used:**

Profit = SP − CP | Loss = CP − SP | Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/af048df6fb3d9d074ebb015e9be9c69eeaf75f098f928a21621aee46d7f0b457.png] 

⇒ Let the **Cost Price** be x.

⇒ Profit = 2200 − x

⇒ Loss = x − 1800

⇒ 2200 − x = x − 1800

⇒ 2x = 4000 ⇒ x = 2000

⇒ New **Profit** = 2050 − 2000 = ₹50

⇒ **Profit %** = (50 ÷ 2000) × 100 = 2.5%

**∴ The correct answer is Profit of 2.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price (MP)

The price printed on the label of an item. **Discount** is always calculated on the **Marked Price**.

Successive Discount

If two discounts d₁% and d₂% are given, the **Effective Discount** = [d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂) ÷ 100]%.

Dishonest Dealer

Profit % = [Error ÷ (True Value − Error)] × 100, where error is the weight difference.
